subject: maths
title: Chapter 9 · Test 3
summary: Chapter 9 test 3: 15 questions on sampling, box plots, standard deviation, scatterplots, time series and evaluating statistical reports.
body: This test covers Chapter 9 · Statistics: collecting data and sampling, box plots and the five-number summary, standard deviation, scatterplots and lines of best fit, time-series data and evaluating statistical reports. It has 15 multiple-choice questions, from easy to challenge. Allow about 25 minutes and work with no notes. A calculator is allowed for this test, but show your working on paper so you can check each step. Many questions use a graph or diagram — read the axes and scales carefully before you answer.

questions.prompt: A school sorts its students by year level, then randomly chooses 10% of the students in each year level. Which sampling method is this?

options.C: Simple random sample from the whole school

questions.explanation: Splitting the population into groups and choosing the same fraction from each group is a stratified sample. It is not systematic — there is no every-k-th rule.
steps: The population is split into groups (year levels) first.
Then a fair share (10%) is chosen from each group — a stratified sample.

mistakes.A: Step 1: systematic means every k-th person on a list. Here the school first splits students into groups.
mistakes.C: Step 1: the students were split into year levels first, and each level was sampled separately.
mistakes.D: Step 1: only 10% of each year level is chosen, not everyone.

questions.topic: Box plots and the five-number summary
questions.prompt: The box plot shows the reaction times of a large group of people. About what percentage of the times are between 42 and 60?
questions.explanation: 42 is Q1 and 60 is Q3, and the box between them holds about 50% of the data. 18 is the IQR, not a percentage.
steps: 42 is the left end of the box (Q1) and 60 is the right end (Q3).
The box holds the middle two quarters: about 50%.

mistakes.B: Step 2: 42 to 60 is the whole box (Q1 to Q3), which is two quarters, not one.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 75% runs from the minimum to Q3. The box alone holds two quarters.
mistakes.D: Step 1: 60 − 42 = 18 is the IQR, a length on the scale, not a percentage.

questions.diagram_alt: A box plot of reaction times on a scale from 25 to 80: minimum 30, Q1 42, median 48, Q3 60, maximum 75

questions.prompt: Which graph is best for showing how a city's population changed each year from 2000 to 2024?

options.A: A pie chart with one sector for each year
options.B: A scatterplot with population on the horizontal axis
options.C: A box plot of the 25 population values
options.D: A line graph with the years on the horizontal axis

questions.explanation: Data recorded over time is a time series, best shown as a line graph with time across the bottom. A box plot loses the order of the years.
steps: Population each year is a time series.
Show it on a line graph with time (years) on the horizontal axis.

mistakes.A: Step 1: a pie chart shows parts of one whole, not change over time.
mistakes.B: Step 2: time must go on the horizontal axis so the graph reads from left to right.
mistakes.C: Step 1: a box plot hides the order of the years, so you cannot see the change over time.

questions.topic: Scatterplots and lines of best fit
questions.prompt: The scatterplot shows shoe size and maths test mark for 16 students. Which describes the relationship?
questions.explanation: High and low marks appear at every shoe size, with no upward or downward pattern, so there is no correlation.
steps: Look for a direction: do the dots rise or fall from left to right?
They are scattered with no pattern, so there is no correlation.

mistakes.A: Step 1: the dots do not rise in a pattern — they are scattered all over.
mistakes.B: Step 1: the dots do not fall in a pattern either.
mistakes.D: Step 1: there is no downward drift; the marks are spread out at every shoe size.

questions.diagram_alt: Scatterplot of maths test mark against shoe size for 16 students; the dots are scattered between 45% and 95% at every shoe size from 5 to 11 with no pattern

questions.prompt: Runner A's 100 m times have mean 12.4 s and standard deviation 0.2 s. Runner B's have mean 12.1 s and standard deviation 0.9 s. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Runner B is faster on average, but Runner A is more consistent
options.B: Runner A is faster on average and more consistent
options.C: Runner B is faster on average and more consistent
options.D: Runner A is faster on average, but Runner B is more consistent

questions.explanation: Runner B's mean time is lower (faster), while Runner A's smaller standard deviation means steadier times. A higher mean time does not mean faster in a race.
steps: In a race, a lower mean time is faster: Runner B (12.1 s).
A smaller standard deviation means more consistent: Runner A (0.2 s).

mistakes.B: Step 1: a LOWER time is faster, and Runner B's mean (12.1 s) is lower.
mistakes.C: Step 2: Runner B's larger standard deviation (0.9 s) means LESS consistent times.
mistakes.D: Step 1 and Step 2: both are reversed — lower time means faster, and smaller standard deviation means more consistent.

questions.topic: Box plots and the five-number summary
questions.prompt: The parallel box plots show the travel times of students who catch a bus or a train to school. How much greater is the median bus time than the median train time?
questions.explanation: Bus median 35 − train median 26 = 9 minutes. The maximums differ by 15, but the median is the line inside the box.
steps: Read the medians (lines inside the boxes): bus 35, train 26.
Difference = 35 − 26 = 9 minutes.

mistakes.A: Step 2: 5 is the difference in the IQRs (13 − 8). Compare the lines inside the boxes.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 15 is the difference in the maximums. Compare the medians.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 2 is the difference in the minimums. Compare the medians.

questions.diagram_alt: Parallel box plots of travel times. Bus: minimum 20, Q1 28, median 35, Q3 41, maximum 55. Train: minimum 18, Q1 22, median 26, Q3 30, maximum 40

questions.topic: Scatterplots and lines of best fit
questions.prompt: For a plant, the line of best fit linking hours of light per week (h) and growth in millimetres (G) is G = 0.5h + 12. The data covers 10 to 50 hours. Predict the growth for 30 hours of light.
questions.explanation: G = 0.5 × 30 + 12 = 15 + 12 = 27 mm, and 30 is inside the data (10 to 50 hours), so this is interpolation. Adding before multiplying gives 21.
steps: Substitute h = 30: G = 0.5 × 30 + 12.
Multiply first: 15, then add 12: G = 27 mm.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you added 30 and 12 before multiplying. Multiply 0.5 × 30 first.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 0.5 × 30 = 15 is only part of it. Add the 12.
mistakes.C: Step 1: you solved 0.5h + 12 = 30 for h. Here h = 30 is given — substitute it.

questions.prompt: The graph shows a Melbourne shop's umbrella sales each quarter for 3 years (Q3 is July to September). Which is the best description?

options.A: Seasonal, with a peak every Q3, and an increasing trend
options.B: Seasonal, with a peak every Q1, and a decreasing trend
options.C: Seasonal, with a peak every Q3, and a decreasing trend

questions.explanation: Sales peak every Q3 (55, 50, 45), so the data is seasonal, and each year is lower than the one before, so the trend is decreasing.
steps: The highest point each year is in Q3: a seasonal pattern.
The Q3 peaks fall from 55 to 50 to 45: a decreasing trend.

mistakes.A: Step 2: compare the Q3 peaks: 55, then 50, then 45 — they are getting lower.
mistakes.B: Step 1: read the labels under the peaks: they are above Q3.
mistakes.D: Step 1: the peak comes in the same quarter each year, so there is a repeating seasonal pattern.

questions.diagram_alt: Time-series graph of quarterly umbrella sales for 3 years: 30, 42, 55, 34, then 28, 39, 50, 31, then 25, 35, 45, 27, peaking in Q3 each year

questions.prompt: A recycling report shows the amount recycled with two squares. The 2025 square is 3 times as wide and 3 times as tall as the 2015 square. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The square looks 9 times as big, but recycling only tripled
options.B: The square looks 3 times as big, and recycling tripled
options.C: The square looks 9 times as big, and recycling increased 9 times
options.D: The square looks 6 times as big, but recycling only tripled

questions.explanation: The area grows by 3 × 3 = 9, so it looks 9 times as big, while the amount went from 50 to 150 tonnes — 3 times. Thinking it looks only 3 times bigger ignores the area effect.
steps: Width × 3 and height × 3 means area × 9: the square looks 9 times as big.
The labels show 50 → 150 tonnes: only 3 times as much.

mistakes.B: Step 1: making BOTH the width and height 3 times bigger multiplies the area by 3 × 3.
mistakes.C: Step 2: read the labels: 50 to 150 tonnes is 3 times as much.
mistakes.D: Step 1: the area is multiplied (3 × 3), not added (3 + 3).

questions.diagram_alt: Two squares on a baseline: a small square labelled 50 tonnes for 2015 and a square three times as wide and three times as tall labelled 150 tonnes for 2025

questions.prompt: A sports club has 1080 juniors, 840 seniors and 480 veterans. A stratified sample of 60 members is chosen. How many seniors should be in the sample?
questions.explanation: Seniors are 840 ÷ 2400 = 0.35 of the club, and 0.35 × 60 = 21. Sharing equally (20 each) ignores the group sizes.
steps: Seniors' share = 840 ÷ 2400 = 0.35.
Seniors in the sample = 0.35 × 60 = 21.

mistakes.A: Step 2: 60 ÷ 3 = 20 gives each group the same number. Each group's share must match its size.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 840 ÷ 60 = 14 divides the wrong numbers. Find the seniors' fraction of 2400 first.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 35 is the seniors' PERCENTAGE of the club. Take 35% of 60.

questions.prompt: The dot plot shows the number of goals a netball player scored in 6 games. Find the population standard deviation, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: Mean 6; squared deviations 9, 1, 0, 0, 1, 9 total 20; σ = √(20 ÷ 6) ≈ 1.83. Forgetting the square root gives 3.33.
steps: Read the values: 3, 5, 6, 6, 7, 9. Mean = 36 ÷ 6 = 6.
Squared deviations: 9, 1, 0, 0, 1, 9 — total 20.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 20 ÷ 6 ≈ 3.33 is the variance. Take the square root.
mistakes.C: Step 3: √(20 ÷ 5) divides by n − 1. Population σ divides by n = 6.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 8 ÷ 6 averages the plain distances. Square each deviation first.

questions.diagram_alt: Dot plot of goals in 6 games on a scale from 0 to 12: one dot each at 3, 5, 7 and 9, and two dots at 6, with the mean 6 marked

questions.topic: Box plots and the five-number summary
questions.prompt: A box plot has minimum 20, lower quartile 35, interquartile range 12 and range 50. Find the upper quartile and the maximum.
questions.explanation: Q3 = Q1 + IQR = 35 + 12 = 47, and maximum = minimum + range = 20 + 50 = 70. Adding the range to Q1 gives 85, which is wrong.
steps: Range = maximum − minimum, so maximum = 20 + 50 = 70.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you added the range to Q1. The range is measured from the MINIMUM: 20 + 50.
mistakes.B: Step 1: Q3 is above Q1, so add the IQR: 35 + 12.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 50 is the range, not the maximum. Add it to the minimum.

questions.prompt: A news story says "The average height of the combined squad is 185 cm", after averaging Team A (12 players, mean 180 cm) and Team B (8 players, mean 190 cm). What is the correct mean height of all 20 players?
questions.explanation: Total = 12 × 180 + 8 × 190 = 2160 + 1520 = 3680, and 3680 ÷ 20 = 184 cm. The story's 185 cm gives the smaller team too much weight.
steps: Total height: Team A 12 × 180 = 2160, Team B 8 × 190 = 1520.
All 20 players: 2160 + 1520 = 3680 cm.

mistakes.B: Step 1: averaging the two means treats the teams as the same size. Team A has more players.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you matched the team sizes to the wrong means. Team A (180 cm) has 12 players.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 180 + 190 is not divided. Find the total height and divide by 20.

questions.topic: Scatterplots and lines of best fit
questions.prompt: The line of best fit on the scatterplot passes through (2, 33) and (10, 73). The data covers 2 to 10 hours of practice. What does the line predict for 0 hours, and how reliable is it?

options.A: 33 words per minute, because that is the first point on the line
options.B: 23 words per minute, and it is reliable because it is the y-intercept
options.C: 43 words per minute, but it is extrapolation
options.D: 23 words per minute, but it is extrapolation, so treat it with caution

questions.explanation: The gradient is (73 − 33) ÷ 8 = 5, so c = 33 − 10 = 23. But 0 hours is outside the data range, so 23 words per minute is extrapolation and may not be accurate.
steps: At 0 hours: 33 − 5 × 2 = 23 words per minute (the y-intercept).
0 hours is outside 2 to 10 hours, so this is extrapolation: treat with caution.

mistakes.A: Step 2: (2, 33) is at 2 hours. Find c, the value at 0 hours.
mistakes.B: Step 3: 0 hours is outside the data (2 to 10 hours), so the prediction is extrapolation.
mistakes.C: Step 2: going from x = 2 back to x = 0 SUBTRACTS 2 × 5 from 33.

questions.diagram_alt: Scatterplot of typing speed against hours of practice from 2 to 10 hours, with a line of best fit through the marked points (2, 33) and (10, 73)

questions.prompt: A time series has four values a, 10, 14, b. Its two 3-point moving averages are 11 and 13. Find a and b.
questions.explanation: (a + 10 + 14) ÷ 3 = 11 gives a + 24 = 33, so a = 9; (10 + 14 + b) ÷ 3 = 13 gives b + 24 = 39, so b = 15. Treating 11 and 13 as the values themselves ignores the averaging.
steps: First average: (a + 10 + 14) ÷ 3 = 11, so a + 24 = 33.
Second average: (10 + 14 + b) ÷ 3 = 13, so b + 24 = 39.
So a = 9 and b = 15.

mistakes.A: Step 1: 11 and 13 are the moving averages, not the missing values. Each average uses three values.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 33 and 39 are the totals of each group of three. Subtract the known values 10 and 14.
mistakes.D: Step 1: you used a + 10 + 14 = 11. The SUM of three values is 3 × 11 = 33.
